newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power steady in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power steady in featureless trade.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West were steady Wednesday in relatively featureless trade, industry sources said.
"There's no news, no weather and no big loads," said one Mid-West trader who was assessing early winter values during the lull in spot trade.
On-peak next day power for a 16-hour block in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was talked steady in the $12.00-15.50 range, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak MAPP power was pegged steady in the $7.50-9.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the sources said.
On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Thursday delivery were said to be holding in the $16.50-19.50 per MWh range.
Off-peak MAIN power was said to be steady in the $9.50-11.00 per MWh range, the sources said.
October MAIN was loosely discussed in the $15.50-18.50 range.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Thursday delivery were quoted steady at $15.00-16.00.
Off peak ECAR was said to be unchanged in the $11.50-14.00 per MWh range.
October ECAR was talked in the $16.50-17.50 range, while November was assessed at $17.50-18.25 and December at $18.25-19.00, the sources said.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Thursday delivery in the north area was assessed steady in the $13.00-15.00 range, while off peak was pegged at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
In the south of SPP, power was pegged at $16.75-17.75, while off peak was assessed near $12.00, the sources said.
October SPP was assessed in the $15.50-17.50 area.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
